rules.title: Interest on security deposits for RSO units
rules.requirement: If your unit is covered by the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, your landlord must pay you interest on your security deposit at the rate the City sets each year. The landlord pays it monthly or yearly, either directly or as a credit against rent, and must tell you in writing which payment method they chose. Waiting until move-out to pay all the interest at once does not meet the rule.
rules.key_value: Interest at the City's annual rate (2025: 4.320%), paid monthly or yearly
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental units in the City of Los Angeles subject to the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (LARSO). Interest has accrued since November 1, 1990.
rules.quoted_span: Interest shall begin accruing on November 1, 1990, on a monthly basis. A tenant shall be given the unpaid accrued interest in the form of either a direct payment or a credit against the tenant’s rent. The landlord shall choose between these two methods of payment and notify the tenant in writing of his or her choice.
rules.penalty: Not stated in the code text. The source says noncompliance is used successfully as a defense in eviction cases.
